# Harness Summary

The harness achieves poor-to-moderate accuracy across three datasets: 37.5% on ds_alpha, 54.2% on ds_beta, and lower performance on ds_gamma (incomplete data). The dominant failure pattern is **label-frequency bias**—the model repeatedly selects high-frequency labels from demonstrations (e.g., "torpra-kakli," "dozi-brapas," "pika-dofle") regardless of input content, despite showing identical shallow reasoning ("Closest demonstrations suggest X"). Performance improves modestly with larger training sets (150 vs. 84 samples yields ~17% relative gain), suggesting the in-context learning mechanism exists but fails to build robust feature-to-label associations. The model's reasoning never adapts—it provides no true semantic analysis, only similarity-based guessing. To improve, focus on either stronger demonstration selection, explicit feature engineering in the prompt, or restructuring how the harness surfaces contrastive examples to overcome the demonstration-set bias.
